transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um, hi. Well... I guess I'm just here because... my eating has been really weird lately. I don't know. Some weeks I just... I barely touch dinner. But then other nights, I'm just standing in the kitchen, eating crackers and sweets after everyone else is asleep. It's just... all over the place.
After you eat those crackers and sweets at night, do you do anything to try to undo it or get rid of what you ate?
No, I... I don't do anything like that. I just go to bed.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most of the time?

I suppose... yeah. I go through stretches where... I don't know, the house just feels kind of gray. And heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table... just feeling empty, I guess. Even if nothing terrible really happened that day. It just... is.
How long have you been feeling this way—this sense of emptiness and the house feeling gray and heavy? Has it been going on for weeks, or longer?

Um... it's been going on for a while, I guess. If I add up all those... gray periods, where I just feel guilty and don't really care about anything anymore... it's probably been about seven months total.

During those seven months, have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt more confident or 'up' than your normal self—or has it mostly been the low mood and emptiness the whole time?

I suppose... no, it hasn't just been the emptiness. There are periods where I feel... bright, I guess. Like I'm unstoppable. 

But... then it shifts. I'll get furious over something really small. Like if my husband moves my paints... or if he asks about a receipt. I just... I get really mad.

When you describe these 'bright' periods where you feel unstoppable, and then the periods where you feel gray and empty—do these feel like they come and go in distinct episodes that last days or weeks at a time, or does your mood shift back and forth more randomly throughout each day?

Um... they last a while, I guess. It's not just a day here or there. 

If I really think about it... over the last couple of years, those times where I feel, you know, unstoppable and taking on too much... they've actually taken up more time than the gray stretches. Or the times when I feel... normal.

During those times when you felt unstoppable and taking on too much, did you ever do anything that caused serious problems—like spending a lot of money you didn't have, getting into conflicts at work or with your family, or anything that made people worried about your judgment or safety?

Um... I don't know about serious problems. I mean, I guess it's caused some issues. 

I'm doing this facilitator training... and I have a private blog. But... I've fallen behind on all of it. During those times, I try to do so much, but my projects... my explanations... they just get really hard to organize. It doesn't make sense when I try to put it together. 

And... my husband, well, there's been tension. It's just made it harder to keep up with our normal routines at home. So... yeah, I guess it's affected things.

During those times when you felt unstoppable and taking on too much, did you need significantly less sleep than usual—like feeling rested after only 3 or 4 hours—or did your sleep need stay about the same?

I suppose... yeah, I don't sleep as much then. 

Three or four hours, maybe. And I wake up feeling... fine. Charged, I guess. I'll get up and start writing for the blog, or trying to plan out my projects, even when it's still dark out. I just... don't need the rest.
